extracted.intended_audience: journalism/media scholars, graduate students, and researchers conducting content analysis of news
extracted.subtask_description: Content-analysis coding scheme for assessing newsworthiness of online news stories using Shoemaker et al.'s seven indicators (three deviance dimensions and four social-significance dimensions). Includes sampling and intercoder-reliability procedures for comparing portal vs. traditional online news sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical deviance
rubrics_metrics.description: A deviance indicator used to see how unusually the news event occurs in the real world (i.e., how unlike ordinary occurrences the event is).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as a nominal/binary variable: existence = 1, absence = 0. Applied at the story level. (Paper reports ~41% Yes in sample.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Social change deviance
rubrics_metrics.description: A deviance indicator measured by how a news event potentially threatens the social status-quo or produces social change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as a nominal/binary variable: existence = 1, absence = 0. (Paper reports ~31.9% Yes in sample.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Normative deviance
rubrics_metrics.description: A deviance indicator measured by how much a news event breaks the laws or policies of a society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as a nominal/binary variable: existence = 1, absence = 0. (Paper reports ~36.4% Yes in sample.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Political significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A social-significance indicator that considers an impact on society related to the government system or international governments’ relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as a nominal/binary variable: existence = 1, absence = 0. (Paper reports ~26.2% Yes in sample.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A social-significance indicator considering impact related to business or market issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as a nominal/binary variable: existence = 1, absence = 0. (Paper reports ~18.5% Yes in sample.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A social-significance indicator used when a news event is related to social norms or traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as a nominal/binary variable: existence = 1, absence = 0. (Paper reports ~32.8% Yes in sample.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Public significance
rubrics_metrics.description: A social-significance indicator that considers how importantly a news event impacts the public's well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded as a nominal/binary variable: existence = 1, absence = 0. (Paper reports ~32.9% Yes in sample.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall newsworthiness classification (Deviance vs Social Significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-part conceptual scheme: newsworthiness assessed under two types — deviance (statistical, social change, normative) and social significance (political, economic, cultural, public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the seven discrete indicators as predictors/variables of newsworthiness; each indicator is coded separately (0/1). The scheme is used to compare news selection across organizational types (portal vs. traditional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis and sampling procedure for coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit of analysis: individual news stories appearing on the main first page of each online news site. Sampling: collect news stories of the day before at a consistent time (noon) across study days; study period in paper: one week (Nov 7–13, 2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect all stories on the first page at the chosen sampling time to control for update frequency. Note potential limitation of short sample window; consider longer periods to generalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding protocol and binary measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the seven newsworthiness indicators was operationalized as a nominal variable with values Yes (1) and No (0) indicating existence or absence of that indicator in a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coders mark 1 if the indicator is present in the story, 0 if absent. The study did not measure intensity; authors note intensity could be measured in future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercoder reliability testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to ensure coding consistency: randomly select a subset of articles for double-coding and compute intercoder reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this study, 80 articles were randomly selected out of 686 and coded by two coders; intercoder reliability was calculated using a correlation formula and reported as .88. Use double-coding and report reliability (method and statistic) when applying the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of medium as independent classification (Portal vs Traditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the news source by organizational type: portal media (e.g., Daum.net) versus traditional newspaper online sites (e.g., Joins.com) to examine organizational influence on news selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use market-share or ranking to select representative sites; treat type of medium as an independent variable when comparing prevalence of newsworthiness indicators. The paper reports statistically significant differences across types for most indicators.
